ASSIGNMENT 1 - AI ROBOTICS CONVERSION AND INVESTIGATION
Measuring Distance and Orientation Using Camera and Lasers
Evaluation date: September 30, 2026
Conversion and testing performed by: OpenAI Codex (AI coding tool)

DELIVERABLE URL
Public code: https://github.com/Amanamin2k6/camera-laser-robotics-conversion
Browser application: see the live application link in the repository README.

ORIGINAL DEMONSTRATION
https://demonstrations.wolfram.com/MeasuringDistanceAndOrientationUsingCameraAndLasers/
Authors: Shiva Shahrokhi and Aaron T. Becker (2016).
The downloaded Mathematica source is preserved in source/original.nb.
The original and this adaptation are attributed as CC BY-NC-SA.

WHAT WAS ATTEMPTED
Codex inspected the actual Mathematica notebook and translated its rotated
rectangular footprint, nearest laser/edge intersections, pinhole projection,
movable object, focal-length control, laser-spacing control and reticule into
HTML, CSS, JavaScript and SVG. The browser version additionally displays exact
simulated depths, recovered depths and a two-distance angle estimate.
It runs independently of Mathematica. This report evaluates the submitted
attempt; the discovered faults were retained so the report describes that code.

Coordinate convention: z is forward depth; x is lateral position. The object
center is (z,x). Its footprint is 1 unit deep and 4 units wide before rotation,
and its vertical height is 2 units. The lasers start at lateral coordinates
+s and -s, so their total separation is 2s. Image coordinates follow the source
notebook's mirrored convention u=-lambda*x/z. All lengths use consistent
arbitrary units. A laser depth is axial depth to an intersection, not Euclidean
camera-to-point distance and not object-center depth.

TEST METHOD AND OBSERVED CASES
The app was opened and actually operated in the Codex in-app browser. Tests
included mouse dragging, keyboard slider increments, typing into number fields,
all three presets, positive/negative rotations, calibration changes, missing
hits, field-of-view boundaries, near-camera configurations, and a 390 by 844
mobile viewport. Graphics were visually inspected and screenshots were saved.
The following are browser observations, not claims based only on reading code.

1. Default: z=3, x=-0.2, theta=0, s=1, lambda=0.5. Both hit depths were
   2.500; image coordinates were -0.20000 and +0.20000; angle was 0.00 degrees.
2. Tilted-face preset: z=5, x=0, theta=30, s=1, lambda=0.5. Depths were
   3.845 and 5.000; image coordinates were -0.13003 and +0.10000; angle 30.00.
3. At theta=-30 with the other tilted-preset values unchanged, the depths
   swapped to 5.000 and 3.845, and the estimate was -30.00 degrees.
4. At theta=60 with z=5, x=0, s=1, lambda=0.5, the depths were 3.268 and
   5.732. The estimate was 50.94 degrees, and the status said both lasers hit.
5. At theta=180 with z=5, x=0, s=1, lambda=0.5, both depths were 4.500
   and the estimate was 0.00 degrees.
6. The One laser misses preset returned left depth 4.500, right No hit,
   and Unavailable orientation. The Edge on preset returned two No hit values.
7. At the default geometry, changing lambda from 0.5 to 1 changed image u
   from +/-0.20000 to +/-0.40000, while recovered depths stayed 2.500.
8. With z=1, x=-0.2, theta=0, s=1, lambda=2, reported depths were 0.500,
   image coordinates +/-4.00000, and angle 0.00. Neither dot was visible in
   the image, whose horizontal bounds are +/-0.8.
9. With z=0.1, x=0, theta=0, s=1, lambda=0.5, the object surrounds the
   camera. The app reported two depths of 0.600. The camera image had no brown
   projected object face, although the top view showed a cuboid.
10. Select-all and type '-30' into the angle number field: it became +30.
    Select-all and type '0.75' into focal length: it became 0.175 in this test.
    In contrast, replacing a field's value in one operation could set -30 or
    0.5 correctly. The typing failure is distinct from the underlying math.
11. Clearing the depth field immediately changed it to 0.1. Entering depth
    99 immediately changed it to 15. Keyboard Right on the s and lambda
    sliders changed their values from 1 to 1.01 and 0.5 to 0.51 respectively.
12. Dragging the default object handle moved the center to approximately
    z=5.839409692997914, x=0.5917894857324888. Both depths updated to 5.339.
13. With s=lambda=0.1, distance labels crowded together at the image center.
    With z=15 as well, the dots had SVG centers 399.65517 and 400.34483, each
    with radius 3, so the two rendered spots overlapped heavily.
14. At 390 by 844, controls and panels stacked without horizontal page
    overflow. The plots were approximately 313 pixels wide, making their
    distance markings and object handle very small.
15. The default projected front face had SVG points (220,210), (220,70),
    (620,70), (620,210): width 400, height 140. Its aspect ratio was 2.857,
    rather than the physical face ratio 4/2=2 with equal image-axis scaling.

INDEPENDENT CALCULATION CHECK
node camera-laser-app/verify.mjs compares the JavaScript polygon-edge method
with a separately implemented analytical ray/oriented-box slab calculation.
All 990 tested laser rays agreed on hit/miss and depth, within 1e-9 units.
The tested grid covered z=3,5,15; x=-4,-0.2,0,2,4; eleven angles including
0, +/-30, +/-60, +/-90 and +/-180; and s=0.1,1,2. The independent reference
uses a tolerance for floating-point edge contact.
Closed-form default and +/-30-degree cases and focal-length scaling also passed.
This supports the ideal intersection calculations. It does not establish UI
correctness, camera visibility, general orientation recovery, or equivalence
to a running Mathematica kernel. Mathematica was not executed for this report.

ALL IDENTIFIED FAULTS / PROBLEMS

1. Invalid angle estimate when hits belong to different faces (robotics error).
   In case 4, theta=60 produced 50.94 degrees. The two intersections lie on
   different cuboid edges. The shared-plane formula measures the connecting
   chord, not either face's inclination. The app's internal geometry records
   the face IDs, but the estimator does not check them. It presents the result
   with the ordinary successful-hit status. A same-face check is needed.

2. Full object orientation is ambiguous (inference limitation).
   Case 5 gives 0 degrees at a 180-degree rotation. That is consistent with
   an undirected planar face's inclination, but it does not recover the full
   signed orientation selected by the object control. Two laser depths cannot
   distinguish all symmetric poses. The interface should explain this ambiguity
   and distinguish selected object rotation from observable face inclination.

3. Off-image laser hits are treated as usable camera measurements (visibility
   error). In case 8, u=+/-4 is outside the stated +/-0.8 bounds and neither
   spot is visible, yet the app reports two recovered distances and an angle.
   These are valid simulated geometric intersections, not measurements the
   depicted finite camera could obtain. No out-of-frame warning is shown.

4. Physically invalid camera/object overlap is allowed (model validation).
   Case 9 places the camera and laser origins inside the cuboid footprint:
   its depth interval is [-0.4,0.6]. The app reports exit-surface distances
   as ordinary measurements. It does not warn about overlap or require the
   object to be in front of the camera. This invalid scene should be excluded
   or explicitly identified, even if the ideal intersection arithmetic works.

5. Camera-plane crossings are not properly clipped (rendering error).
   In case 9 the top-view object remains visible but the camera image contains
   no projected brown face. Faces with a corner at or behind the near plane
   are skipped wholesale instead of clipping their visible portions. There
   is no explanation that the projection is invalid. This accompanies the
   unsupported near-camera configuration in fault 4.

6. Unequal image-axis scaling distorts the cuboid (graphics error).
   Case 15 confirms the default front face is drawn at aspect ratio 2.857,
   although its projected physical width/height ratio is 2. The renderer uses
   500 SVG units per horizontal image unit and 350 per vertical unit. The
   source demonstration's camera graphic uses equal coordinate scaling.
   The numeric horizontal u calculations can be correct while this picture
   is geometrically distorted.

7. Negative values cannot be entered reliably by ordinary typing (UI bug).
   Selecting and typing '-30' produces +30. Every input event immediately
   converts and rewrites the field; an intermediate minus sign is treated
   as an empty number and replaced. Negative angles/lateral positions are
   available through sliders or whole-value replacement, but ordinary typing
   loses the requested sign.

8. Decimal typing changes the requested number (UI bug).
   Typing focal length '0.75' produced 0.175 in case 10. Immediate clamping
   and rewriting of intermediate input states interferes with decimal entry.
   The field needs to preserve draft text until a valid value is committed.

9. Clearing an input unexpectedly changes the scene (UI bug).
   Case 11: clearing object depth immediately set it to the minimum, 0.1.
   Clearing is normally part of entering a replacement number, but here it
   moves the object into a problematic near-camera configuration before the
   replacement is finished. Empty drafts should not be interpreted as zero.

10. Out-of-range values are silently replaced (UI limitation).
    Entering 99 for depth becomes 15 immediately, without explaining that
    the value was constrained. Preventing excessive values is useful, but a
    user can believe the requested value was accepted unless they notice the
    replacement. Clamping should be explained or validated on commit.

11. Dragging exposes excessive precision and disagrees with slider steps (UI
    consistency). Case 12 puts long fractional strings into the narrow number
    fields while sliders use 0.01 steps and display rounded values (5.84 and
    0.59). Dragged values need consistent rounding/display; the computation
    may retain more precision internally. The long strings are hard to read.

12. The distance reticule is frequently unreadable (graphics/UI bug).
    Case 13 shows many labels piled up at the vanishing point. Even default
    long-distance labels crowd together. The original source adapts its
    reticule scale based on lambda*s; this attempt uses a fixed label list.
    It needs adaptive ticks, label culling or zoom to support small spacing
    and focal length. Merely having labels in the SVG is not functional reading.

13. Overlapping spots still yield an apparently exact estimate (sensor-model
    limitation). At z=15, s=lambda=0.1, the two rendered centers are only
    0.68966 SVG units apart, but each radius is 3. They visually merge, while
    the table still gives two independent exact simulated distances and an
    angle. No finite sensor resolution or separation confidence is modeled.
    This is an ideal-model limitation, not a failure of the algebraic inverse.

14. Minimum rendered dot size is not a physical spot-size model (graphics
    limitation). In case 13 a forced minimum radius keeps dots visible as
    distance increases. Their apparent size no longer follows the perspective
    shrinkage used for nearer spots. The diagram should identify this as a
    visibility aid rather than imply physical laser-spot size accuracy.

15. Mobile plot labels and drag target become too small (responsive UI).
    At approximately 313 pixels plot width, nominal 14-unit SVG text becomes
    about 5.5 screen pixels tall and the 16-unit handle diameter about 6.3
    pixels. The page fits horizontally, but the reticule is difficult to read
    and the object handle is difficult to acquire. Numeric controls remain
    usable. Mobile rendering needs a larger plot/zoom or accessible annotations.

16. Mobile users must scroll through controls before seeing any result (layout
    limitation). At 390 by 844, the first screen contains the title and most
    controls; neither plot nor measurement results are visible. Adjusting a
    control and seeing its graphical effect requires substantial scrolling.
    A compact control layout or nearby summary would make exploration easier.

17. Important original visual annotations are omitted (conversion fidelity).
    The conversion has an angle slider and textual offset/focal-length labels,
    but lacks the original orientation dial, object angle arc, and s/lambda
    dimension arrows in the top view. The replacement control works, yet
    readers cannot directly see those geometric relationships as in the source.

18. The perspective floor grid is missing (conversion fidelity).
    The original camera view draws a projected floor grid and horizon/ground
    regions. The attempt draws a flat tinted lower half instead. The cuboid
    and spots are visible, but the original perspective depth cues are absent.

19. The top-view window clips allowed object positions (display limitation).
    At center depth z=15, even an unrotated object extends to 15.5, beyond
    the fixed visible range. Lateral positions near +/-4 can also clip it.
    The entire object is not always visible, and there is no zoom/pan control.
    The fixed range is inherited from the original, but the new numeric
    controls make these clipped scenes particularly easy to select.

20. Individual source-download links do not provide a runnable bundle
    (delivery/UI limitation). The footer offers HTML, app.js and style.css,
    but omits the imported geometry.js module and favicon.svg. The downloaded
    HTML also depends on relative file names and must be served over HTTP
    for native modules. Downloading only those offered files is insufficient.
    Downloading the complete repository and following its README does work.

21. Displayed rounded image coordinates do not reproduce the full-precision
    recovered values exactly (numeric presentation limitation). The table
    rounds u to five decimal places but computes depth from unrounded u.
    In the far-distance case it shows u=-0.00069; using that displayed value
    gives 0.01/0.00069=14.49275, while the app displays 14.500. This difference
    is rounding, not an inverse-formula error, but the precision relationship
    is unexplained and matters for independently checking the measurements.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS

1. The app loads and runs in a normal JavaScript browser without Mathematica,
   API keys or package installation. The local static-server test produced
   both views, controls, measurements and source links. No console warnings
   or errors were captured during the exercised local scenes.

2. The default scene matches the source defaults: center (3,-0.2), theta=0,
   laser offset 1, focal length 0.5 and the 1-by-4 rectangular footprint.
   Visual inspection showed the camera, two lasers, cuboid and object handle.

3. Actual pointer dragging works. Case 12 moved the handle and updated
   the cuboid, the numeric position controls, rays and measured depths.
   This is observed interaction, not just the presence of a pointer handler.

4. The object rotation control changes the top-view cuboid and camera
   projection. Whole-value setting and slider operation support positive and
   negative angles. Cases 2-5 exercised several rotations; typing has the
   separate failure documented in fault 7.

5. Laser-spacing and focal-length controls respond, with source ranges
   0.1 through 2. Keyboard Right incremented both sliders by 0.01, and the
   companion number fields updated. Minima and maxima were exercised.

6. Reset scene works. After changed controls and presets, it restored
   z=3, x=-0.2, theta=0, s=1 and lambda=0.5 and the default outputs.

7. All three test-scene buttons work and produce their intended inputs:
   a 30-degree front face, one missing laser, and a 90-degree narrow footprint.
   They make the documented cases reproducible without manually changing
   every parameter.

8. The nearest forward laser intersection calculation works for the
   independently checked valid scenes. All 990 tested rays matched the
   analytical oriented-box calculation, including misses and rotated objects.
   This finding is limited to the tested grid and ideal geometric model.

9. Default axial depths are correct: the center is at 3 and the front
   face is 0.5 closer, so both laser depths are 2.5, not 3. This distinction
   between center depth and surface depth is correctly preserved.

10. The mirrored horizontal pinhole projection is correct in the tested
    in-frame cases: u=-lambda*x/z gives -0.2 for the +1 laser and +0.2 for
    the -1 laser at depth 2.5 and lambda=0.5. The two red dots appear on
    the corresponding opposite image sides.

11. Focal-length scaling works. Case 7 doubled lambda and doubled the
    magnitudes of u, widened the projected object and narrowed the top-view
    field-of-view cone, while leaving physical intersection depths unchanged.

12. Recovering depth from full-precision simulated u works: z=-lambda*x/u.
    Default and tilted cases recover their forward intersection depths. The
    independent tests also checked recovery for every nonmissing grid hit.
    This is mathematical consistency, not a validation with external sensor data.

13. The shared-face angle calculation works when its assumption is satisfied.
    At theta=+30 it gives +30; at theta=-30 it gives -30; default parallel
    face gives 0. The +/-30 results agree with closed-form face equations.

14. One-hit and zero-hit states are handled correctly in the tested presets.
    The app shows No hit, em dashes for unavailable readings, a useful status
    message and Unavailable angle. It does not invent a finite second distance
    or show a NaN angle in these cases.

15. The camera graphic places in-frame red spots, a vanishing point and
    distance ticks at the expected horizontal positions. For example, with
    s=1 and lambda=0.5, depth 2.5 corresponds to |u|=0.2, between the depth-2
    and depth-3 ticks. Tick readability and vertical shape scaling have the
    separate limitations already listed.

16. Numeric controls and sliders synchronize on committed whole-value
    changes. The table, measurement cards and status update without a page
    reload. Range clamping prevents unlimited depth/focal-length values,
    although its communication and draft-input behavior are faulty.

17. Basic responsive layout works: at the tested mobile size, panels stack,
    numeric controls remain operable, and no horizontal page overflow was
    observed. This does not mean the scaled SVG annotations are mobile-readable.

18. The project supplies readable standalone source, the preserved original
    notebook, attribution, reproduction instructions, screenshot evidence and
    an independent verification script. These make the conversion inspectable
    and allow another person to repeat the investigation.

EVIDENCE AND REPRODUCTION
evidence/default-app.jpg - default desktop scene.
evidence/cross-face-angle.jpg - misleading 60-degree scene output.
evidence/out-of-frame.jpg - camera image with no observable red dots.
evidence/camera-inside-object.jpg - camera-plane rendering failure.
evidence/reticule-crowding.jpg - distance labels at small s and lambda.
evidence/mobile.jpg - full mobile layout.
evidence/browser-observations.json - recorded browser observations.
evidence/geometry-check.txt - independent numerical verification output.

The report is plain text. Screenshots support it but are not required to read
its enumerated faults and working features. Findings cover the exercised cases;
they do not claim exhaustive testing of every continuous parameter combination,
browser, device or real optical system. No claim is made that a student
personally performed the AI's recorded tests.
